title: ShanHai Gateway: Open-Source Multi-Upstream LLM Router
summary: ShanHai Gateway is a new Go-based multi-upstream LLM gateway enabling developers to route requests across multiple AI providers with load balancing.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- ShanHai Gateway launched today as an open-source Go-based gateway for routing LLM requests across multiple upstream providers.
- The tool provides load balancing, failover capabilities, and unified API access to multiple AI model providers simultaneously.
- Developers can now manage multi-provider LLM infrastructure with a single lightweight gateway written in Go for performance.


ShanHai Gateway, a new open-source multi-upstream LLM gateway written in Go, launched today on GitHub. The tool enables developers to route API requests across multiple large language model providers with built-in load balancing and failover capabilities. Developer ffseika0304 released the project to address the growing need for unified infrastructure when working with multiple AI model vendors simultaneously.


## Core Architecture and Routing Capabilities


The gateway functions as a reverse proxy layer between applications and LLM providers, allowing developers to configure multiple upstream endpoints in a single deployment. Written in Go for performance and low resource overhead, ShanHai Gateway supports simultaneous connections to providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and other API-compatible services. The architecture prioritizes request routing efficiency while maintaining compatibility with standard OpenAI API formats.


Key technical features include dynamic upstream selection based on availability, automatic retry logic for failed requests, and configurable timeout settings per provider. The Go implementation offers faster request processing compared to Python-based alternatives, making it suitable for high-throughput production environments.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially launched on November 12, 2026, ShanHai Gateway is available now through its GitHub repository under an open-source license. The initial release includes comprehensive documentation for deployment, configuration files for common provider setups, and examples demonstrating multi-provider routing patterns. Developers can clone the repository and deploy the gateway to their own infrastructure without vendor lock-in.


## Load Balancing and Failover Features


The gateway implements several strategies for distributing requests across upstream providers. Round-robin distribution ensures even load across available endpoints, while weighted routing allows developers to prioritize specific providers based on cost or performance characteristics. When an upstream service experiences downtime or returns errors, the gateway automatically redirects requests to healthy alternatives without exposing failures to end-user applications.


- Automatic health checking for upstream endpoints with configurable intervals
- Circuit breaker patterns to isolate failing providers temporarily
- Request queue management during traffic spikes
- Detailed logging of routing decisions and provider performance metrics


## Developer Use Cases and Integration


ShanHai Gateway addresses common challenges in multi-provider LLM deployments. Organizations building AI applications often need redundancy across multiple vendors to manage rate limits, reduce costs through provider arbitrage, or ensure availability during outages. The tool provides a single integration point that abstracts provider-specific details while maintaining full control over routing logic.


Integration requires minimal changes to existing codebases that already use OpenAI-compatible APIs. Developers point their API clients at the gateway endpoint instead of direct provider URLs, then configure upstream providers through YAML or JSON configuration files. The gateway handles authentication token management for each provider and translates responses into standardized formats when needed.


## What This Means


The launch of ShanHai Gateway reflects the maturing ecosystem around LLM infrastructure tooling. As enterprises adopt multiple AI providers for different use cases, demand grows for sophisticated routing and orchestration layers. This open-source approach gives developers full control over their multi-provider architecture without relying on commercial gateway products. The Go implementation choice signals a focus on performance-critical applications where latency and resource efficiency matter. Organizations evaluating multi-provider strategies now have a production-ready foundation for building resilient LLM infrastructure.
